name: Two-Wheel Moped (L1e-B)
description: The EU's two-wheel moped, which takes in the speed pedelec: a light two-wheeler of no more than 4,000 W and 45 km/h that isn't a powered cycle. It needs EU type approval and an AM licence, and motor insurance when its motor can propel it on its own.

restrictions.rule: Needs EU type approval: it may be sold, registered or put into service only with the manufacturer's certificate of conformity, and carries the manufacturer's statutory plate

A speed pedelec, an L1e-B cycle designed to pedal, weighs 35 kg or less in running order, has pedals that can propel it on the rider's leg power alone and an adjustable riding position, and its motor adds no more than four times the rider's pedal power
A speed pedelec's frame, front fork, seat-post and handlebar stem must pass the bicycle tests of ISO 4210:2014, at the delegated regulation's minimum forces
The manufacturer must fit features that stop its powertrain being tampered with to raise its power, torque or maximum design speed
Riders need an AM moped licence, or a licence of any other category, which also covers AM; the minimum age is 16, which a member state may lower to 14 or raise to 18

Riders need an AM moped licence, which covers two-wheelers up to 45 km/h and 4 kW of maximum net power, or a licence of any other category; the minimum age is 16, which a member state may lower to 14 or raise to 18

Needs third-party motor insurance covering personal injury and property damage when it's propelled exclusively by mechanical power with a maximum design speed over 25 km/h; a speed pedelec whose motor only assists pedalling isn't, so the Directive leaves its insurance to member states
restrictions.citation: Directive 2009/103/EC, Arts. 1(1), 3, as amended by Directive (EU) 2021/2118; Directive (EU) 2021/2118, recitals 4, 6

restrictions.rule: The Court of Justice, asked about a speed pedelec, held that a bicycle whose motor only assists pedalling isn't a vehicle under the Motor Insurance Directive
restrictions.citation: Judgment of 12 October 2023, KBC Verzekeringen, C-286/22
